chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'By what is the rescued one recognised?' He said: 'The one whose deed corresponds to his word — for him the testimony is affirmed. And the one whose deed does not correspond to his word — that (faith) is merely entrusted (temporary).'

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةَ: The testimony of faith (shahada) — confirmed as genuine and enduring for the one whose deeds match his words
key_terms.النَّاجِي: The rescued/saved one — one who has attained genuine salvation through sincere faith confirmed by righteous action
key_terms.مُسْتَوْدَعٌ: Entrusted/deposited — a technical term in Shia theology referring to faith that is granted temporarily and may be withdrawn; contrasted with 'mustaqarr' (established) faith

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq distinguish between genuine and temporary faith in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: The Imam al-Sadiq (AS) is asked how one can identify the truly saved person — one whose faith is genuine and enduring. His answer draws a sharp distinction between two types of believers: the one whose actions align with his professed beliefs, and the one whose actions contradict his words. The former is confirmed in his testimony of faith (shahada), while the latter possesses only a 'deposited' or 'lent' faith — a temporary gift that may be taken back, indicating a precarious spiritual state.
